N-3.1-A.skill: compare kinetic energies when both mass and speed differ, and avoid confusing kinetic energy with momentum or with speed alone.

N-3.1-B.skill: treat kinetic energy as a scalar: change in K depends on the speeds only, not on the direction change or the vector change in velocity.

N-3.2-A.skill: find the work done by an individual force when several forces act and the object moves at constant speed or along an incline, using net work and angle correctly.

N-3.2-B.skill: compute work from a force that changes with position (area with sign) and connect it to a change in speed.

N-3.3-A.skill: read force direction and motion from potential-energy data: force is the negative slope of U, and total energy limits the motion.

N-3.3-B.skill: find changes in potential energy that depend on configuration (height, compression, reference level) rather than on path length or arbitrary zeros.

N-3.4-A.skill: apply energy conservation with nonconservative work, and recognize which quantities do and do not depend on the path.

N-3.4-B.skill: choose the right states and geometry (height, spring compression, loop condition) when applying conservation of mechanical energy.

N-3.5-A.skill: distinguish work from power and use efficiency, slope and time to compare energy transfer rates in multi-step settings.

N-3.5-B.skill: use P = Fv with the force component along the velocity, constant-power engines and instantaneous versus average power.
